messages:
Ana (acme-infra): Hey team, seeing intermittent streaming failures from our editor plugin since this morning. Clients get a broken pipe / ECONNRESET and some sessions show as 5xx on our billing dashboard. Happening ~1-2% of streams.
Ravi (support): Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste one request_id + approx timestamps? Are you using the JS SDK, Python SDK, or raw HTTP?
Ana (acme-infra): request_id=rix:0a1b2c3d, observed ~1765454205-1765454212 UTC. Using our Go proxy -> Redwood hosted API (streaming chunked). Repro curl attached below.
Ana (acme-infra): ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream```
Lina (devex): Thanks. Quick sanity: does your proxy buffer/chunk or close client connection early? We often see NAT/proxy idle timeouts that close the client, then gateway logs show upstream reset and it gets classified as a 5xx.
Marco (sre): Adding logs from our side for that request_id: gateway shows `upstream_connection_reset` and then `response_classified_502`. Looks like client half-closed during chunk flush. Can you share your proxy timeout and TCP keepalive settings?
Ana (acme-infra): Our proxy (envoy) has idle_timeout=60s, keepalive probes default. Most of these streams run under 45s. No explicit half-close in our app.
Ravi (support): Two immediate asks: 1) can you test with keepalive enabled from client -> proxy (TCP keepalive shorter, e.g., 15s) and 2) try forcing a final zero-length chunk / explicit stream termination so gateway doesn't guess.
Marco (sre): Repro tip we use: run a tight loop that opens a streaming session, reads a few chunks, and then closes socket abruptly:
```python
# quick repro (client abort)
import requests
s = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json_payload, stream=True)
for i, line in enumerate(s.iter_lines()):
    if i==2:
        s.close()  # simulate client abort
        break
```
This triggers the same upstream reset in our lab and the gateway sometimes marks it 502.
Lina (devex): If you can't change client runtime, temporary mitigation: fallback to non-streaming endpoint for long-poll UX, or add a short heartbeat chunk every 10-15s from client to keep connection 'active'.
Ana (acme-infra): Ok we'll try keepalive + heartbeat. One more: how will this affect billing? We have users flagged as 5xx in billing.
Ravi (support): We'll exclude confirmed client-abort cases from billing. Please forward the request_ids and exact UTC windows for those samples and we'll run an audit. If logs show `client_closed_connection` we won't bill.
Marco (sre): Long-term fix ideas: 1) improve half-close detection (differentiate FIN vs RST), 2) bump gateway grace window before classifying 5xx, 3) add instrumentation to propagate client socket state into accounting. We're tracking in ENG-4281.
Ana (acme-infra): Thanks. We'll test and send 10 sample request_ids this afternoon.
deploy-bot: New ticket created #SUP-9821: "client-silence probe -> possible misclassified 5xx" assigned to Marco.
Ravi (support): Thanks @Ana — once you send samples we'll expedite the billing audit and share a short runbook for your engineering team to reduce false positives. :thumbsup:
Ana (acme-infra): sending now, appreciate the quick help :heart:
